proof_nl: Fix an arbitrary real number x, and let m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m <= x < m + 1. Define f = x - m. Then 0 <= f < 1, and x = m + f. Since frac(x) denotes the fractional part of x, we have frac(x) = x - floor(x) = f. Therefore x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1. This holds for every real x, so the lemma is proved.
